hypothesis: After an extreme 15m return, price partially mean-reverts due to temporary order-flow imbalance (forced/impatient flow) rather than information.
entry_rules: z=r_15m/stdev(r,96 bars ending t-1); long z<=-k, short z>=+k; k in {2.5,3.0,3.5}. No other indicators.
exit_rules: target=50% retracement of event move; stop=1.5x event range on MARK price; time stop 8 bars; same-bar stop+target resolves to stop.
position_sizing: risk-normalised: all results in R units, R=1.5x event range
cost_assumptions: Delta India per-symbol maker/taker x1.18 GST + 2bps slippage; funding charged at snapshot crossings; stop and time exits always taker.
reason: Gross expectancy is negative (-0.0401R) BEFORE costs, so the mean-reversion hypothesis is false at these thresholds rather than merely uneconomic. Strategy significantly UNDERPERFORMS the exposure-matched random null (-0.0243R, t=-3.10). Negative in all 4 symbols, all 7 quarters, all 3 chronological splits, and all 21 execution/parameter cells.
notes: Win rate 61.7% but mean negative: the pre-registered target (0.5x event move) is at most 1/3 of the pre-registered stop (1.5x event range), so break-even needs ~75% wins. Maker fills unverifiable without book data; optimistic and conservative both reported and differ trivially (-0.0810 vs -0.0828).

hypothesis: SUPERSEDES H-Scalp-1. Same hypothesis (15m extreme-return mean reversion), re-run after fixing a same-bar target look-ahead bug.
exit_rules: unchanged, plus: on a maker entry bar only the adverse outcome may trigger (the favourable extreme generally preceded the fill)

parameters.bugfix: same-bar target on maker entry bar disallowed

reason: Bug fix made it worse, as expected: gross -0.0539 (was -0.0401), net -0.0973 (was -0.0828). Negative BEFORE costs; loses to its null (t=-4.76); negative in all symbols, quarters and splits.
notes: The original H-Scalp-1 record remains in the registry; this supersedes it with corrected figures. Verdict unchanged.

hypothesis: An extreme 15m directional move reflects persistent directional order flow; price retraces (offering a passive entry) and then CONTINUES in the direction of the original displacement.
entry_rules: z=r_15m/stdev(r,96 ending t-1); z>=+k long, z<=-k short. Passive limit at close_t - retest*(close_t-open_t). Cancel if price retraces 100% (through open_t) or after 8 bars unfilled. Bar spanning both entry and invalidation -> skipped.
exit_rules: R = entry - open_t = (1-retest)*|move|, so the stop IS the structural invalidation. target = entry + 1.0R, stop = 1.0R, time stop 8 bars, same-bar resolves to stop, maker entry bar cannot register a target.
cost_assumptions: Delta India per-symbol maker/taker x1.18 GST + 2bps slippage; stop and time exits always taker; funding at snapshot crossings

baseline_result.null_at_extreme: strategy -0.0211 vs null +0.1689 (but that null enters at the realised bar low = look-ahead, unachievable)
baseline_result.note: the three nulls disagree; null design is ambiguous for a limit-entry strategy, so the null comparison is NOT decisive here

reason: Gross expectancy is POSITIVE (+0.1156R) and positive on all four symbols, so the continuation mechanism has real signal -- unlike H-Scalp-1, which was negative before costs. But cost/R is 0.1359 against a 0.1156 gross edge, so the mechanism does not pay for itself: net -0.0214R, 95% CI [-0.0606, +0.0159], t_adj -0.92. Matches the pre-registered condition "positive before costs, negative after realistic costs".
notes: Same-bar target look-ahead bug found and fixed BEFORE classification; pre-fix the grid showed +0.482R at t=32 for retest=0.50, which was entirely artifact (356 of 425 target exits occurred on the entry bar vs 1 stop). OOS unstable: train +0.034, valid -0.075, test -0.024. Quarterly net R flips sign repeatedly. Not classified FRAGILE/EXECUTION-DEPENDENT because it is not profitable under ANY execution assumption, including the most favourable.

hypothesis: Volatility compression followed by confirmed expansion, entered passively on a retest of the broken boundary, produces continuation with a gross edge large enough to survive Delta India costs.
entry_rules: 15m ATR(14)/close below trailing 20th percentile (960-bar causal window); >=4 consecutive compressed bars; range/ATR<=1.5. 5m expansion: close beyond boundary AND body>=0.5*ATR(5m) AND volume>=1.5x 20-bar average. Arm A: passive limit at the broken boundary, 3-bar lifetime, never converted to taker. Arm B (diagnostic): taker at the next bar open.
exit_rules: stop = opposite compression boundary (skip if >2% of entry); target 2R (3R secondary); time stop 24 x 5m; same-bar stop+target resolves to stop; a passive fill bar cannot register a target.
position_sizing: 0.5% equity risk per trade, $10k per symbol, leverage cap 10x (never bound)
cost_assumptions: Delta India per-symbol maker/taker x1.18 GST + 2bps slippage; stop and time exits always taker; funding charged at snapshot crossings

baseline_result.note: Strategy beats all three nulls by +0.39 to +0.46R (t 4.4-5.2), but every null sits near -0.8R because this tiny-R 2R geometry placed at random times is catastrophic. Beating a catastrophic null while being negative is not evidence of edge.

out_of_sample.test: LOCKED - gate refused, PROMISING criteria not met

reason: Gross expectancy negative on BOTH train and validation for BOTH execution arms (A: -0.081 / -0.155; B: -0.056 / -0.028), with t_gross between -0.2 and -1.0, i.e. indistinguishable from zero. Decisive: at ZERO cost the net is still -0.097R, so this is not an economics problem. 0 of 48 sufficiently-sampled grid arms produced positive net expectancy on validation.
notes: The Arm A/B execution comparison was informative and cuts the OPPOSITE way to H-Scalp-2: both arms fail by a similar margin, so execution is NOT the bottleneck here - the signal is absent. Structural finding: cost/R is 0.28-0.39, far worse than H-Scalp-2's 0.136, because the stop IS the compression range and compression zones are tight by construction. Tighter compression gives a better signal but a smaller R, so the hypothesis is self-defeating on costs. QA: 23 tests, 0 skips, covering causal-percentile, perturbation and same-bar look-ahead checks.

hypothesis: Extreme perpetual funding reflects leveraged crowding, so the crowded side experiences poor forward returns. Arm A: pure carry (short on high funding, long on low). Arm B: funding extreme PLUS evidence price has stopped continuing in the crowded direction.
entry_rules: funding >= expanding 95th pct -> SHORT; <= 5th pct -> LONG (min 500 prior observations, shifted one bar so no current/future data is used). Entry at the OPEN of the first 1H bar starting strictly after the funding bar closes (signal_time + 3600). Arm B additionally requires an adverse prior return over the lookback, no new 6h extreme, and a 1H close reversal -- all evaluated on bars strictly before entry.
exit_rules: fixed 24h hold (48h/72h in the grid). No stop; carry is the thesis.
position_sizing: 3x leverage cap (deliberately low), $10k/symbol; results reported in bps of notional
cost_assumptions: taker entry + taker exit x1.18 GST + 2bps slippage per side = 15.8 bps round trip; funding accounted separately at settlement instants

baseline_result.note: DECISIVE. The strategy is statistically indistinguishable from all three nulls: vs vol-matched random timing +2.17 bps (t=0.20); vs RANDOMISED SIGN -0.63 bps (t=-0.06); vs funding shifted 14d against price -1.97 bps (t=-0.18). Null B is the killer -- randomising the direction implied by crowding changes nothing, so the crowding direction carries no information. Null C failing means the funding/price relation is not causal.

out_of_sample.note: gross sign flips between splits: train +8.36 -> valid -11.16

robustness.funding_persistence: entry percentile ~0.51-0.79 holds flat to +24h; carry IS collectable

reason: Fails the pre-registered falsification clause. The strategy is indistinguishable from all three nulls, including randomised sign (t=-0.06) and funding decoupled from price (t=-0.18). Gross also flips sign between train (+8.36 bps) and validation (-11.16 bps), and even at ZERO cost the pooled gross is only +2.95 bps per 24h trade. 2 of 36 grid arms positive on validation, which is below chance.
notes: IMPORTANT NUANCE: the funding CASH FLOW is real and collectable -- positive on all four symbols (+2.5 to +7.7 bps) with confirmed persistence. What is absent is any predictive relationship between funding extremes and forward PRICE returns. Carry is real; the crowding signal is not. The long side illustrates it: it collects the most funding (+9.65 bps) and loses the most on price (-20.14 bps) -- you are paid to stand in front of a falling market. The short side has genuinely positive gross (+11.0 bps) but the 15.8 bps taker round trip consumes it. DATA PATHOLOGY documented pre-run: 21-44% of funding observations sit exactly at +/-0.01% (the interest-rate baseline), and for BTC/ETH the 95th percentile IS that pin, so the pre-registered '>= p95' fires on ~31% of bars. Both '>=' (pre-registered) and strict '>' were reported; the strict variant cut Arm A train from 980 to 211 trades and did not change the verdict. QA: 22 look-ahead/convention tests, 0 skips, covering all 7 required proofs.

hypothesis: XAUT and PAXG are perpetuals on the same metal, so temporary relative-price dislocations should converge, producing a tradable relative-value edge independent of gold direction.
entry_rules: spread = log(XAUT) - beta*log(PAXG), beta from causal rolling OLS (20d, window ending t-1). z = (spread - rolling mean)/rolling std, 20d causal. z >= +2.0 -> short XAUT / long PAXG; z <= -2.0 -> reverse. Entry on the NEXT bar; no same-bar fills.
exit_rules: z returns to 0 (0.5 secondary); max hold 24h (48h secondary); stop |z|>=3.5
position_sizing: hedge-ratio weighted legs, 0.5% risk, 3x max leverage, $10k
cost_assumptions: Delta metals fees are IDENTICAL maker and taker (0.01% each = 1.18 bps after GST), so the A/B/C execution comparison differs only in slippage and fill probability. Pair round trip = 4.72 bps fees + slippage. Funding accounted per leg at 4h settlements. Legging cost charged when only one leg fills.

baseline_result.note: Nulls corrected mid-experiment to carry the SAME funding exposure as the strategy; the first version omitted it and was meaningless given a ~52 bps/day carry. Corrected: vs random timing with the same hedge, strategy-null = +2.41 bps, t=0.88 -- NOT significant, so the convergence TIMING adds nothing. vs randomised sign the strategy is 63.2 bps WORSE (t=-21.6), because a random sign averages the funding differential to zero while the strategy systematically takes the expensive side.

robustness.funding_differential: XAUT +25.2 bps/day, PAXG -9.0 bps/day => pair carries +/-52 bps/day
robustness.fill_sensitivity: net -74 to -89 bps across fill probabilities 1.0 -> 0.3

reason: Overdetermined failure. (1) Convergence does not outperform a mechanically fair null: vs random timing with identical hedge and funding, t=0.88. (2) The pair carries +/-52 bps/day of funding differential against a convergence edge of ~15.7 bps -- carry exceeds the entire edge by ~3.3x and is directional, so the same trade is heavily penalised one way. (3) Realised gross convergence was only +1.51 bps because 0% of trades converged inside the 24h hold, the spread half-life being 24.6h. (4) Only 12 trades in 116 days; 0 of 36 grid arms had >=5 validation trades.
notes: The spread IS statistically mean-reverting (AR(1) coefficient -0.028, autocorr 0.972 -> 0.684 over 48h, stable hedge ratio beta ~0.978). The hypothesis fails not because the statistical premise is wrong but because reversion is too slow to capture and the funding differential dwarfs it. IMPORTANT COROLLARY: the same measurement implies a PURE CARRY trade -- always short XAUT / long PAXG -- would collect ~+52 bps/day. That is a different hypothesis (directional carry, exposed to spread widening), was NOT pre-registered here, and must not be inferred as validated from this experiment. Power was unreachable by construction: 116 days = 0.32 yr, so even Sharpe 2.0 gives t = 1.13. Stated before results. QA: 19 look-ahead tests, 0 skips, covering all 9 required proofs.

hypothesis: With 5m and 1m trend regimes aligned, ADX/DI confirming strength and Williams %R confirming momentum, price has enough short-term continuation edge to profit from entering WITH the trend. No pullback, no retracement, no oversold recovery.
entry_rules: 5m (last CLOSED bar): Supertrend aligned, ADX(28)>=25, DI aligned. 1m: Supertrend aligned, ADX(28)>=25, DI aligned, WPR(140) beyond -80/-20 and moving in the trend direction vs the previous closed bar. Entry at the NEXT 1m open. Frozen: ST(10,2.0), ADX 28, DI 14, WPR 140.
exit_rules: Structural stop: min(Supertrend, lowest low since the Supertrend last flipped) for longs, mirrored for shorts, closed bars only. Target 2R (3R diagnostic). Same-bar stop+target resolves to the stop.
cost_assumptions: taker entry + taker exit x1.18 GST + 2bps slippage/side; funding at settlements

baseline_result.null: random timing matched on side, stop distance and 2R geometry: null -0.4163R vs strategy -0.3785R, diff +0.0488, t=1.90 (not significant). Limitation: a random entry is not conditioned on a trend regime, so holding-period and volatility exposure differ.

pullback_comparison.reading: removing the pullback raised trade count 726x (6 -> 4356) and made the hypothesis measurable for the first time; it did NOT raise gross expectancy.

robustness.per_symbol: 3/4 positive gross, all tiny (max +0.0296, t=0.92); none significant
robustness.long_short: symmetric: long +0.0111, short +0.0101 -- no directional dependence
robustness.quarters: 3/6 positive gross; all positives in 2025H1, all negatives from 2025Q4

ablation.note: train gross; removing WPR (Arm B) IMPROVES it

robustness.stop_definition: structural leg-low stop median 0.672% with cost/R 0.383 vs legacy min(ST,low) 0.238% with cost/R 1.06 -- the structural stop cuts cost/R by 64%
robustness.wpr_variant_C: 5 trades on train, 0 on validation -- uninterpretable

reason: Applied literally, the pre-registered rule (§16) gives NO ECONOMIC EDGE: train gross is positive (+0.0317) but far below the 0.3827 transaction cost. HOWEVER this label overstates the gross signal and must not be read as equivalent to H-Scalp-2. The gross edge is NOT statistically distinguishable from zero (t_gross +1.20 train, -0.94 valid), is NEGATIVE out of sample, is positive in only 9 of 16 months, and beats a matched random null by only t=1.90. The substantive reading is NO SIGNAL.
notes: PRIMARY FINDING (§20). The pullback requirement was NOT the cause of the original failure. Removing it increased trades from 6 to 4,356 on train (726x) and from 1 to 1,504 on validation, making the hypothesis measurable for the first time -- and the measurement shows gross expectancy of approximately zero, negative out of sample. The pullback had been concealing the absence of edge behind an unmeasurably small sample. The Supertrend + ADX + Williams %R concept lacks edge as a family, with or without a pullback. Ablation confirms WPR subtracts value: Arm B (no WPR) has HIGHER train gross (+0.0577, t=2.11) than Arm A (+0.0317, t=1.20). Useful engineering finding: the structural leg-low stop cuts cost/R from 1.06 to 0.38 versus the legacy min(ST,low) stop used in all earlier experiments -- a 64% reduction that still was not enough. UNIVERSE CORRECTION: run on the corrected 4-symbol universe (XRPUSD included at 1.43% synthetic over the study window). §19 audit: 20 tests, 0 skips, incl. 5m-closed-bar projection, causal structural stop, and a trade-level perturbation test.

hypothesis: Multi-timeframe trend alignment confirmed by ADX/DI contains a genuine gross continuation edge without any pullback or Williams %R condition.
entry_rules: 5m (last CLOSED bar): Supertrend aligned, ADX(28)>=25, DI aligned. 1m: Supertrend aligned, ADX(28)>=25, DI aligned. Entry at the NEXT 1m open. Frozen ST(10,2.0), ADX 28, DI 14, threshold 25. No WPR, no pullback, no added filter.
exit_rules: validated structural leg-low stop; 2R target (3R diagnostic); same-bar resolves to stop
position_sizing: 0.5% equity risk, $10k/symbol, 3x leverage cap (identical to prior experiments)
cost_assumptions: taker/taker x1.18 GST + 2bps slippage/side; funding at settlements

baseline_result.primary_question: 1m confirmation adds NO statistically established gross information: gross(A)-gross(B) = +0.0400 train (t=1.53) and +0.1814 valid (t=1.92), both CIs straddling zero. Its real contribution is STOP GEOMETRY: cost/R 0.40 for Arm A vs 5.04 for Arm B, because median stop widens 0.147% -> 0.674%.

robustness.per_symbol: 4/4 positive gross pooled, but every t below 1.16 -- none significant
robustness.long_short: short +0.0539 (t=1.64) vs long +0.0077 (t=0.24); the majors FELL over this window, so a short-biased apparent edge is consistent with drift rather than signal
robustness.quarters: 3/6 positive gross; every positive in 2025Q1-Q3, every negative from 2025Q4
robustness.component_attribution: gross: A +0.0577 (t=2.11) > D +0.0443 (t=2.31) > C +0.0339 (t=1.34) > B +0.0177 (t=0.95). cost/R: A 0.40 < C 0.52 < D 1.80 < B 5.04. The 1m Supertrend is what controls cost, because it defines the leg the structural stop is measured from.

reason: Pre-registered rule §23: Arm A gross is +0.0577 on train but -0.0431 on validation, and the rule classifies NO SIGNAL when either segment is <= 0. Every one of the four arms is negative on validation (A -0.043, B -0.225, C -0.012, D -0.069). The train t_gross of 2.11 is below the t>=3.2 this program requires given its accumulated search, and the gross that does appear is concentrated on the short side during a falling market.
notes: §22 ANSWER. Removing Williams %R improved the TRAINING SAMPLE but did not reveal a persistent trend signal: train gross rose +0.0317 -> +0.0577 and t_gross 1.20 -> 2.11, while validation gross stayed NEGATIVE in both (-0.0505 -> -0.0431). Combined with H-WPR-1, the Supertrend + ADX/DI + Williams %R family is now closed from both directions: the pullback was not the problem, and neither was Williams %R. USEFUL ATTRIBUTION: the 1m confirmation earns its place through stop geometry rather than prediction -- it improves cost/R more than twelvefold (5.04 -> 0.40) without a demonstrable gain in gross expectancy. Any future trend work on this venue should treat entry filters as risk-geometry selectors first and signal second. Universe: corrected 4 symbols, eligibility over the complete study window. §21 look-ahead audit re-run before results: 20 tests, 0 skips.

The original run used a 3-symbol universe because XRPUSD was excluded by a recent-30-day liquidity pre-filter (6.82% synthetic) rather than by the study-window measure (1.43%). Arm A: passive limit at the broken boundary, 3-bar lifetime, never converted to taker. Arm B (diagnostic): taker at the next bar open.
